items.q: A 3-year-old child accidentally aspirates a peanut while laughing. Bronchoscopic inspection is most likely to reveal the aspirated foreign object lodged in which airway?
o: Right main bronchus or right intermediate bronchus
items.exp: The right main bronchus is wider, shorter, and runs more vertically than the left main bronchus. Aspirated foreign bodies therefore enter the right bronchial tree far more frequently.
r: Correct. The right main bronchus is more vertical and wider, predisposing to foreign body lodgement.
Incorrect. Left main bronchus is narrower, longer, and more horizontal.
Incorrect. Left upper lobe is angled sharply away from the carina.
Incorrect. Solid foreign bodies typically pass through the tracheal lumen into a bronchus.
items.kp: Aspirated foreign bodies preferentially enter the right main bronchus due to its wider caliber and more vertical orientation.

items.q: At which surface anatomical landmark does the trachea bifurcate into right and left primary bronchi?
o: Sternal angle of Louis (T4-T5 vertebral level)
items.exp: The trachea bifurcates at the carina, corresponding surface-wise to the sternal angle of Louis (manubriosternal joint) and the T4-T5 intervertebral disc level.
r: Correct. Tracheal bifurcation occurs at the sternal angle of Louis at T4-T5.
Incorrect. Xiphisternal joint corresponds to T9.
Incorrect. Jugular notch corresponds to T2.
Incorrect. Cricoid cartilage marks tracheal origin at C6.
items.kp: Tracheal bifurcation occurs at the carina, aligning with the sternal angle of Louis and T4-T5 intervertebral level.

items.q: During emergency surgical tracheostomy, which endocrine structure crosses anterior to the second, third, and fourth tracheal rings and must be retracted or divided?
items.exp: The isthmus of the thyroid gland crosses anteriorly over the 2nd, 3rd, and 4th tracheal rings in the lower anterior neck.
r: Correct. The thyroid isthmus overlies the 2nd through 4th tracheal rings.
Incorrect. Thymus gland lies lower in the anterior superior mediastinum.
Incorrect. Parathyroid glands lie on the posterior thyroid capsule.
Incorrect. Submandibular gland lies in the digastric triangle.
items.kp: The thyroid isthmus crosses directly anterior to tracheal rings 2 to 4, representing a key landmark during tracheostomy.

items.q: What type of cartilage composes the 16 to 20 C-shaped structural rings of the trachea?
items.exp: The C-shaped rings of the trachea are composed of hyaline cartilage, providing rigid structural support against negative intrathoracic inspiratory collapse.
r: Correct. Tracheal rings are composed of hyaline cartilage.
Incorrect. Elastic cartilage is found in the epiglottis and ear pinna.
Incorrect. Fibrocartilage is found in intervertebral discs.
Incorrect. Calcified cartilage is a pathological or senescent state.
items.kp: Hyaline cartilage forms the 16 to 20 C-shaped rings of the human trachea.

items.q: Contraction of which smooth muscle band bridging the posterior gap of the tracheal cartilage rings reduces tracheal diameter to increase airflow speed during coughing?
items.exp: The trachealis muscle spans the posterior gap of the C-shaped cartilages. Contraction narrows the lumen, accelerating linear air velocity during explosive coughing.
r: Correct. Trachealis muscle contracts to narrow airway caliber and boost cough clearance velocity.
Incorrect. Cricothyroid tenses vocal cords.
Incorrect. Sternothyroid is an extrinsic strap muscle.
Incorrect. Bronchialis is an anatomical misnomer.
items.kp: The trachealis smooth muscle spans the posterior tracheal wall, narrowing luminal diameter to enhance cough velocity.

items.q: How many independent bronchopulmonary segments are present in the normal right lung?
items.exp: The right lung possesses 10 bronchopulmonary segments: 3 in the upper lobe (apical, anterior, posterior), 2 in the middle lobe (lateral, medial), and 5 in the lower lobe (superior, medial, anterior, lateral, posterior basal).
r: Correct. The right lung has 10 bronchopulmonary segments across 3 lobes.
Incorrect. 8 segments is typical of the left lung due to fused basal segments.
Incorrect. 12 segments is an overcount.
Incorrect. 7 segments is an undercount.
items.kp: The normal human right lung contains 10 distinct bronchopulmonary segments, each supplied by an independent tertiary bronchus.

items.q: What is the key difference in vascular anatomy between pulmonary arteries and pulmonary veins regarding bronchopulmonary segments?
o: Pulmonary arteries run intrasegmentally with bronchi; pulmonary veins run intersegmentally in septa
Pulmonary veins run intrasegmentally; pulmonary arteries run intersegmentally
Both vessels run together inside the segmental bronchus lumen
Pulmonary arteries drain into the left atrium directly
items.exp: Pulmonary arteries follow the branching bronchial tree within the center of each segment (intrasegmental), whereas pulmonary veins course through the intersegmental connective tissue septa.
r: Correct. Pulmonary arteries course intrasegmentally with bronchi; pulmonary veins run intersegmentally between segments.
Incorrect. Veins are intersegmental, not intrasegmental.
Incorrect. Vessels never run inside the bronchial lumen.
Incorrect. Arteries originate from the right ventricle.
items.kp: Pulmonary arteries run intrasegmentally alongside tertiary bronchi, whereas pulmonary veins run intersegmentally in septal planes.

items.q: The internal cartilaginous ridge that separates the openings of the right and left primary bronchi at the tracheal bifurcation is called the:
items.exp: The carina is the prominent sagittal ridge of cartilage projecting upward at the bifurcation of the trachea into mainstem bronchi, densely innervated by cough reflex receptors.
r: Correct. The carina is the mucosal ridge dividing the tracheal bifurcation.
Incorrect. Conus elasticus forms the vocal ligament.
Incorrect. Thyroid notch is on the thyroid cartilage.
Incorrect. Interarytenoid fold lies in the posterior larynx.
items.kp: The carina is the highly sensitive internal ridge marking the bifurcation of the trachea into primary bronchi.

items.q: Which cranial nerve provides parasympathetic secretomotor and bronchoconstrictor innervation to the tracheobronchial tree?
items.exp: The vagus nerve (CN X) provides parasympathetic preganglionic fibers via the pulmonary plexus, releasing acetylcholine to induce smooth muscle bronchoconstriction and stimulate mucus secretion.
r: Correct. Vagus nerve innervates tracheobronchial smooth muscle and submucosal glands.
Incorrect. Glossopharyngeal supplies carotid sinus and pharynx.
Incorrect. Accessory supplies SCM and trapezius.
Incorrect. Phrenic provides somatic motor innervation to the diaphragm.
items.kp: The vagus nerve mediates parasympathetic bronchoconstriction and submucosal secretomotor function via muscarinic receptors.

items.q: What respiratory epithelial cell type secretes surfactant-like uteroglobin (CC16) and acts as a progenitor for airway repair in small terminal bronchioles?
items.exp: Club cells (formerly Clara cells) are non-ciliated dome-shaped cells in terminal bronchioles that secrete uteroglobin (CC16), detoxify harmful inhaled compounds via cytochrome P450, and regenerate airway epithelium.
r: Correct. Club cells secrete protective secretoglobins and regenerate ciliated bronchiolar epithelium.
Incorrect. Type I pneumocytes mediate alveolar gas exchange.
Incorrect. Goblet cells secrete thick mucin.
Incorrect. Kulchitsky cells are neuroendocrine cells producing serotonin.
items.kp: Club cells in terminal bronchioles secrete CC16, detoxify toxins, and serve as stem cells for bronchiolar repair.
